| Code-index adapter seam | partial | Opt-in, default-off seam letting a downstream repository expose derived structural source facts (symbols, blast radius, affected tests, route inventory) to repo-local gates and lints through a swappable provider adapter. Targets the "coverage asserted from a hand-written list rather than derived from the file surface" defect class, where a gate emits an absolute correctness claim about a scope it does not cover and stays green. Contract is 8 verbs — `symbols`, `impact`, `affected`, `routes`, `indexed` (JSON array) and `status`, `freshness`, `sync` (JSON map) — plus a provider-free `selftest <verb>` shape mode and a `capabilities` map declaring each verb's support level. Provider unavailability exits 1 and MUST NOT be conflated with a neutral empty value, so a consumer can never report clean for an unindexed repository; `freshness` exits 2 for STALE, and an adapter that cannot determine freshness MUST exit 2 rather than claim fresh. Two providers ship — `codegraph` (broad language coverage, real freshness and test-impact) and `codebase-memory` (indexes shell, which codegraph cannot parse, so it is the only provider that sees this framework's own source; declares `affected` and `freshness` unsupported rather than approximating them). PARTIAL because the seam, its resolver, both providers, the hermetic contract selftest, the doctrine skill, and the downstream recipe all ship and validate, and one consumer (`test-impact-shadow.sh`) is wired but is deliberately ADVISORY-ONLY — it reports a would-have-skipped figure and never gates, exits only 0 or 2, and no exit code encodes "safe to skip". No GATING consumer exists: reachability nudges for the integration-completeness family and an impact-aware validation map remain unbuilt, and adoption is per-repo via `codeIndex.adapter`. | swe-agent, graphrag | [docs/recipes/use-a-code-index.md](../recipes/use-a-code-index.md); [skills/bubbles-code-index-adapter/SKILL.md](../../skills/bubbles-code-index-adapter/SKILL.md); [docs/CATALOG.md](../CATALOG.md) | `bubbles/adapters/codeindex/`<br>bubbles/adapters/codeindex/none.sh, bubbles/adapters/codeindex/codegraph.sh, bubbles/adapters/codeindex/codebase-memory.sh, bubbles/scripts/codeindex-resolve.sh, bubbles/scripts/codeindex-resolve-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/codeindex-adapter-contract-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/test-impact-shadow.sh, bubbles/scripts/test-impact-shadow-selftest.sh, skills/bubbles-code-index-adapter/SKILL.md | — |
| Evidence-backed experience recall | shipped | Relevance retrieval over Bubbles-owned structured experience -- compacted RESULT-ENVELOPE history, anchored lessons, owner decisions, findings, and outcomes -- without promoting any of it to current authority. Targets the "prior incident is retained but unfindable" defect class, where a repository already holds the record of a problem it is about to repeat. Every hit is authority tier 4 and permanently `recallAuthority: advisory`; a valid source anchor never promotes the hit, so a caller must independently re-read the source before relying on it. The authority boundary is MECHANICAL, not advisory prose: result-envelope-validate.sh refuses any envelope citing a recall record id, the recall index directory, or a content-classified recall export in an evidence field, and refuses it in every mode including --advisory. Repository isolation is structural rather than documented -- the public twin derives repository root and alias from its own install location and refuses --repo-root, --repository-alias, and --adapter -- so cross-repository recall is not expressible. The corpus is closed: raw host transcripts, chat logs, terminal scrollback, arbitrary Markdown, source text, and inferred personas are inadmissible, and unanchored legacy lessons are excluded from recall while remaining valid skill-evolution input. Two providers ship: `none` (the default, which returns empty and changes no behavior anywhere) and `local-lexical` (deterministic, standard-library only, no network, no model, no daemon). Retrieval quality is measured rather than asserted -- a labeled corpus records macro precision and recall at the result bound, and a document-frequency guard plus relevance floor raised measured macro precision from 0.54 to 1.00 with recall held at 1.00. | claude-code, graphrag | [docs/recipes/evidence-backed-experience-recall.md](../recipes/evidence-backed-experience-recall.md); [docs/CATALOG.md](../CATALOG.md); [docs/CHEATSHEET.md](../CHEATSHEET.md) | `bubbles/adapters/experience-recall/`<br>bubbles/adapters/experience-recall/none.sh, bubbles/adapters/experience-recall/local-lexical.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-resolve.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-index.py, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-lifecycle.py, bubbles/schemas/experience-record.schema.json, bubbles/eval/fixtures/experience-recall/corpus.json, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-resolve-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-adapter-contract-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-index-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-cli-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-lifecycle-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-authority-selftest.sh, bubbles/scripts/experience-recall-eval-selftest.sh, agents/bubbles_shared/experience-recall.md | — |
